text:
anya: quick sync — post-launch backlog surgeon. we need to pick top 3 things for the 0.1.1 ship (no big infra changes). can we decide async here?

mike: ok — can you list candidates?

anya: short list: 1) streaming latency regression fix (customer A high impact) 2) high-priority UX enhancement: inline token-cost display 3) improve batcher heuristics for bursty traffic (cost win) 4) reranker tuning for search relevance 5) small telemetry cleanups (missing trace ids)

rajesh: streaming latency reg is a bug we should treat as P0. customers seeing tail-latency spikes after the canary.

sophia: +1 for trace ids — blocked debugging on a couple of incidents. but low user-facing impact.

alex: batcher heuristics could reduce token cost ~20% for some workloads. needs benching but low-risk code changes.
mike: reranker tuning needs offline eval and a short AB test — longer than our minor release window.

anya: proposed prioritization: (A) fix streaming latency (B) batcher heuristics (C) inline token-cost display. reserve a quick follow-on for trace ids if we get extra cycles. thoughts?

rajesh: concur on A. for B we should gate on perf bench: if bench shows <10% win, kick to next sprint.
sophia: can we ship inline cost as a feature flag? small frontend + API change, can be dark-launched.

alex: I can prototype batcher change in a branch today and run perf jobs tomorrow. ETA for results: 48hrs.

mike: engineering capacity check: we have 3 dev-days this sprint for infra-adjacent work. A likely needs hotfix branch + patch release. B prototype + bench, C frontend + API flag. Feels tight but doable if we split tasks.

anya: plan: 1) create hotfix branch for streaming latency. rajesh + mike to triage, target patch release within 24-36h. 2) alex to run batcher perf and post results in this thread. if result >=10% cost reduction -> allocate dev-days to implement; else defer. 3) sophia to own inline cost flag: prototype PR, dark launch, release note opt-in. 4) trace ids as backlog groom item for next sprint.

rajesh: I'll open the hotfix PR now and add a short regression test. tagging @mike for review.

mike: got it. I'll do the review and coordinate a staging deploy.

deploy-bot: deploy queued — staging build 0.1.0-rc5 (sha: ab12f3c) — target: staging — started by mike

alex: perf job kicked off: run id batcher-171555 — will paste numbers when done.

sophia: I'll sketch the UI copy for the token-cost display and send a quick design for feedback.

anya: acceptance criteria for the release: 
- streaming latency regression mitigated (measured tail p95/p99 improvements)
- batcher: only included if perf >=10% cost improvement and no error/regression in throughput
- inline cost: feature-flagged, dark-launched, no client-visible defaults changed
- release notes + rollback plan documented in the PR

mike: add QA checklist: run synthetic traffic, check KV cache TTLs, validate fallback model routing still stable.

rajesh: initial hotfix PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/patch/streaming-tail-fix — PTAL

alex: perf results: batcher baseline -> 120 tokens/sec; prototype -> 147 tokens/sec (+22.5%). memory ~+2%. I'll attach raw logs to the PR.
sophia: design sent, looks good for dark launch. small copy tweak suggested.

anya: excellent — given perf >=10% we include batcher heuristics. next steps: 
- mike: create release branch and coordinate staging smoke (today)
- rajesh + mike: push hotfix, run canary, monitor p99 for 6h
- alex: raise PR for batcher change, include perf artifacts
- sophia: PR for inline-cost UI + feature flag, dark launch only

mike: I'll start the release branch now. ping me if you see any regressions on staging.

deploy-bot: staging deploy succeeded — build 0.1.0-rc5 (sha: ab12f3c) — status: success

anya: thanks all. I'll update roadmap tracker and close this async thread once releases are green. if anything blocks, call a 15m huddle. :thumbsup:
